Where the tree actually stands
First, a correction to what I had carried in: the tree is further along than my notes said. I had Slice 43 / spec v1.28 / 1157 tests. dump.txt and claude-terminal.txt say Slice 45 delivered, spec v1.30, 1162 tests predicted and 1162 observed — green, including the 17 E2E scenarios, ci_local.sh --with-all --with-e2e, and five consecutive MenuEventLogTests runs (the F-95 UUIDv7 monotonic fix holding under repetition, which was the honest check Slice 45 asked for).

So there is no count deviation to chase. All 349 files reconstructed from dump.txt and SHA-256 verified against the exporter's own manifest — zero mismatches.

What I'd found on the dump-size question
Content is 6,014,918 bytes across 349 files; the dump is 6,377,323 — so ~362 KB is per-file metadata overhead. The concentration is severe:

file	size	share
docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md	829 KiB	13%
docs/TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION.md	425 KiB	7%
docs/DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md	220 KiB	3.5%
per-file metadata blocks	~354 KiB	5.5%
LICENSE (verbatim AGPL text)	34 KiB	0.5%
BUILD_PROGRESS.md is the one worth acting on, and it splits cleanly: # M6 Slice 40 begins at byte 743,090 of 848,925. Cutting there archives 726 KiB and retains 103 KiB (slices 40–46 plus a new pointer preamble). Combined with trimming the metadata block down to relative path / size / SHA-256 — dropping absolute path, mtime, permissions, owner, inode, hard links, MIME type and last-commit, none of which a session uses — and eliding the LICENSE body, that's roughly -930 KiB, about 15%, taking 87% capacity to around 74%.

The design constraint I want to flag before building it: a file that export.sh truncates is a file I can no longer deliver as a full file without destroying history. So the archive must be a separate real file (docs/progress/…), excluded by path the way docs/llm/ already is, named in the dump header, and linked from the retained document — plus a small contract test asserting that every excluded document is linked from a dumped one, so the archive can't be silently forgotten.

What I'd resolved for the menu
Stage 3a — ResequenceMenuSectionsAsync — is the next slice, and the plan already specifies it fully: whole-list permutation (not a pairwise swap, because equal positions are permitted), refuse a non-permutation as a stale page, FOR UPDATE over all rows ordered by identifier, one reordered event per section that actually moved, outcome enum Resequenced / NoChange / MenuSectionSetChanged. Slice 45's F-95 fix was its precondition and is now green, so it is unblocked.

I'd traced everything it touches: MenuSectionAdministration.cs (681 lines, the five existing verbs' shape), MenuWorkflow.cs (520 lines, conditional-publish rule), AdministrationMenu.razor (376 lines — the <details class="menu-group" open> groups, and the comment block at lines 46–54 that promises this cut and will need rewriting), the .menu-group-* CSS at app.css:1700–1800 plus its one min-width: 48rem rule at 2449, ManageMenuSection.razor's EditForm method="post" + @formname + PRG pattern the buttons must follow, and HandheldReach.cs's reach selector — currently .menu-group-actions a, which means F-93's obligation bites: up/down are <button>s, so .menu-group-actions button joins the selector in the same slice or the barrier stops asserting anything about the control.

Two census numbers must move with it: §16.4 line 1297 states MenuSectionAdministrationTests at 20 assertions and line 1307 states MenuWiringTests at 19 — TestingSectionContractTests compares both against the files, so a stale one fails loudly.

What I need from you to finish
I hit the tool limit mid-survey, before writing anything. I have the verified tree in the container and a complete plan, but no archive yet — and I'd rather tell you that than hand you a half-built one.

Two things worth deciding, because they change what I build next:

Split the slice or not. Slice 45's own plan argued "one change, one green run, then the feature" — and Slice 46 as scoped is a new write verb with new event semantics plus a documentation restructuring that gates read. If it comes back red, there are two candidate causes, which is exactly the expense that argument was about. My inclination is to ship the dump reduction alone first (no new behaviour, mechanical, immediately drops you off the capacity ceiling), then Stage 3a against a smaller dump with a clean attribution. But it's your call, and the counter-argument — that the dump reduction touches no C# and so can't plausibly redden a menu test — is real.

The LICENSE elision is a veto candidate. Eliding a licence file's body from an LLM export is defensible (it's unmodified AGPL-3.0, and the SHA still pins it), but it's the kind of thing that looks wrong later in an AGPL project whose /source page is a compliance surface. It's worth only 34 KB. Say the word and I'll drop it from the plan.

If you'd rather I just proceed on my own judgement, say "continue" and I'll ship the dump reduction as Slice 46 — full files, structured .tar.gz, docs/progress/ listed as needing git add, no bespoke scripts — with Stage 3a as Slice 47 immediately after.
